blocks.content: kubectl top shows live CPU and memory usage for nodes or Pods.
top gives a current, real-time snapshot of actual CPU and memory consumption, immediately useful for spotting unexpected load.

blocks.alt: A live, current snapshot of real resource consumption

blocks.content:
kubectl top pods
kubectl top nodes

code.content:
kubectl top pods
kubectl top nodes

codes.bash:
kubectl top pods
kubectl top nodes

blocks.content: top nodes gives a cluster-wide capacity view, top pods narrows in on specific workload consumption, the two natural scopes this command operates at.

blocks.alt: A cluster-wide view, or a workload-specific one, the two natural scopes

blocks.content: This command has a hard dependency on Metrics Server, covered in the Autoscaling module, and the full observability context around it is covered in the Observability module's dedicated topic.

blocks.alt: A real prerequisite, and full context, both covered in their own dedicated modules

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: kubectl top shows live CPU and memory usage, scoped to either nodes (cluster-wide) or pods (workload-specific).
It requires Metrics Server to be running, covered as a real prerequisite in the Autoscaling module.
